When it's set on automatic mode, an automatic weapon can fire at least, according to what I know, it can fire a short burst of three to five bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So am I correct in concluding from your answer that in semi-automatic mode, the gun can be fired as rapidly as someone is able to pull the trigger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, drawing your attention to the point in time where you -- when you first hear a shot, can you describe again for us how -- what you do, what happens to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: When I heard the first shot, my body, whether instinctively, or I don't know how, I don't know what happened, anyhow I ended up in the water, I threw myself into the water; and I came to be in such a position that I turned relative to the initial standing position looking towards the river, namely when I fell into the water, I had turned by 180 degrees. So my head was then facing the bank of the river when I was in the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was your head in the water when you had reached this position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. My entire body was in the water and my head was -- it was partly in the water but not all of it, because this was a part of the bank that was -- where the water was not that deep, so I was submerged partly and partly above the surface of the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was someone lying on top of you. What part of your body was someone covering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: The top part of my body -- actually Hasan Mutapcic was lying over the top part of my body, the bottom part of his body was over the top part of my body. Check and the other part of his body covered VG-032.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said at some point, when you thought it was safe, you -- you got up. I'm sorry, if I could ask you a question before that, you mentioned hearing something, some reference made, to six other men. When did you hear that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: This was en route towards the river, because Lukic said that they had to hurry up because there were another six people that they had to get and that had to be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who did you believe those six people were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see them, but I heard actually Hasan Mutapcic who was executed at that spot had told me that his son had remained at that house, and I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that the house in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after you felt it was safe to get up, did you look around and look at the other men who were down at the river? The other Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to determine the extent of their injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I couldn't see their injuries because they were in water, but I could see their bodies. Except for the injury on the body of Hasan Mutapcic who was lying on his back, on top of us; and he had been hit in the back of the head and had an injury there, and his lower jaw was dislocated, the right-hand side of it. That I could see clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The men that were in the water, can you describe your observations about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. All of them lay there with their heads in the water. They were lying on their stomachs, all the four bodies, that is, Ekrem, Meho Dzafic, Hasan Kustura and Amir Kurtalic. While Hasan Mutapcic was lying on his back in contrast to the rest of them, with conspicuous wound that I -- with the wound that I have described.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have any doubt that they were dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No, I had no doubt, not for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who did you leave with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: When I looked around to see whether the situation was safe for me to leave the spot, VG-032 also got up, as I was looking around; and we left the spot together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the details of the path you took from the scene are not essential for the Chamber in adjudicating the facts of this event but can I ask to you tell us where did you go and how long did it take you to get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: When we left the scene, we set out towards the village of Musici, which is I believe some 2.5 kilometres distant from that spot. There we waited for night and for an opportunity to cross the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you finally reach the other side of the river safely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We crossed the river using a tree stump.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you at some point able to get word to your wife that you had survived and that she should come and join you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. If I remember correctly, I believe that was three days after this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd ask that the witness be shown 65 ter 163. It's an aerial photograph. If I could ask the usher to assist the witness, I will be asking the witness to make a few markings on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness VG-014, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. It is quite clear that this is the Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to, with the assistance of the usher, take a pen, and can I ask you before you make any markings on the photograph, to put in the lower left-hand corner VG-014 so we know that it's you that's making the markings and today's date, the 10th of July? And you can use that just as an ordinary pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: [Marks]. Today is the?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: 10th of July, 2008. Can I ask to you draw a circle and put a P in it to show us where the Passat parked when you arrived at the Vilina Vlas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks] A bit closer over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you put a P next to that circle to indicate that that's the Passat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I ask you to do the same for the Yugo, show us where the Yugo was parked and put a Y or a J, I believe, in your language, Yugo is spelt with a J, if would you put a circle and some indication, either Y or J, that it's a Yugo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, could I ask that this be tendered as an exhibit, a Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit P2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask now that the witness be shown 65 ter 164?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel kindly wait for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry. Could I ask that VG-014 be shown 65 ter 164?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-014, I ask you to take a look at 65 ter 164 and ask you do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. One can quite clearly see here the spot to which we have been taken where the crime started, was committed, and the section of the road that we passed from Vilina Vlas to that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does it fairly and accurately depict the Sase junction and the relationship of the road to the Drina River and the places that you've testified about this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to once again put your VG-014 and today's date in the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This photograph was taken quite recently. Is there anything that you see in this photograph that appears to you to be different from as you remember it at the time that you were in Visegrad and particularly on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. Obviously this photograph shows that a lot of time had elapsed, the willows have overgrown the spot, there is more vegetation, and this meadow, this field over here, seems to have changed, I believe. I'm not quite sure because of the scale of this photograph. One cannot notice what it has been sown to, but there are some differences and there are some new house that is have been built since, so it is not the same place. I mean the one shown on this photograph and the place that we were at on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say the willows have grown, are you referring to the trees that run along the bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to draw an X through any of the houses that you know were not there at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I now ask you, you've testified that the cars pulled up on the road and parked. Can I ask you to once again draw a circle with a P in it to indicate where the Passat parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to do the same with respect to the Yugo, a circle and a Y or a J to indicate where the Yugo was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I now ask you to draw a line indicating the path that the cars took to get to this spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. So when we set out from the Vilina Vlas Hotel, we took this road. [Marks] We reached the Sase junction, took the right-hand turn and moved on for about some 200 metres until we reached our destination, namely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you've also mentioned that there was a conversation between Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic about a house. Is that house depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is on the right-hand side above the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle that house, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've also testified that the men were forced to walk towards the river. Could I ask you to draw as best you're able the path that the men took from the cars to the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And ask I ask to you draw seven circles to indicate the approximate location of the men along the river bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can I ask you to indicate where you were in that line of men by drawing a line from the circle that represents you and writing "VG-014"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour at this time I would tender this exhibit as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would become Exhibit P3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you arrived in The Hague this week, were you asked to view -- to look at a video in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise the video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you present when that video was made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does that video accurately depict the path that you and the other men were taken down to the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could ask the Court Officer to switch us to the Sanction system, I'd like to play that video now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to see it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is clearly shows the house about which Lukic asked Vasiljevic whether it was a Muslim house. This is the meadow that -- where the path was which we took to descend to the Drina River but of course there is a difference in that photograph now relative to the time then when we were taking that path, because the meadow -- this is the meadow, this is the plot, but it had been sown to potatoes at that time and this one now has been sown to maize. Yes, this is again the house in respect of which Lukic asked Mitar Vasiljevic whose house it was. Yes. This is the spot where the crime was committed. The bank of the Drina River. But the water table at that time was lower relative to this here shown in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How do you know that the water table was lower at the time, or is different than what we are looking at now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Because this photograph shows that the water has already flooded the surrounding trees on the banks of the river Drina but then on the 7th of June, when this execution was committed, the bank was between five and six metres high. It was not covered with water.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Five and six metres wide.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the road, the path.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While you were walking down this path, were you able to see Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic were standing on my right-hand side, and they were escorting the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender that video, Prosecution 65 ter number 89, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just need one clarification. We received the video which is much more longer than this couple of minutes which we saw right now. And this video also contains some clips related to some other locations, Visegrad, I'm wondering is it admitted just this portion of video or the whole video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is this an abridged version that we saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the video when this video was made it was made at several locations. It is our intention during the course of the trial to show the portion that is each witness can speak to. VG-014 is unable to talk or say anything about the other portions of the exhibit. I'm happy to have the entire exhibit introduced at this time if that's more convenient for Defence counsel and Chambers, but it was my intention to do it as the witnesses appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I consider it more convenient to do it in the manner that you have suggested, in relation to each witness. Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my proposal is portion by portion, per locations, because maybe we will have some objections we cannot raise right now about the whole video, if we have any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour for the clarity of the record, I can give the Court the time code of what portion was shown in court and is now being introduced or is now being tendered in evidence, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I consider it more sensible to tender the portion of the video to which the evidence in court is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That was my intention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So for the purposes of the record in terms of the entire exhibit 65 ter 163 this was 14 minutes and 50 second the to 17 minutes and 55 seconds. That's the portion of the overall video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Does that help you, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Please move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-014, can I ask you now to look around the courtroom and tell us whether you recognise anyone in the courtroom here today apart from me. If you do, I would ask you to take your time, be sure that you do, in fact, recognise them before you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. I shall begin with the gentleman on your right-hand side. I think, to the best of my knowledge of him, that that is Sredoje Lukic. The gentleman in the blue suit and the white shirt is Milan Lukic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say you think, are you unsure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. I am sure, a hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there anything about his appearance here today that strikes you as being different from what you remember back in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, then, the one who was there then was slightly slimmer. Now, this gentleman here has a bit more weight, but he's not difficult to recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person you identified as Sredoje Lukic, what colour jacket is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I believe that this is some kind of a grey colour and the shirt is blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I did not know him as well as I knew Milan Lukic, because he worked as a policeman; so I would occasionally see him in town, and I remember no other details about him except that I knew him as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he have any involvement in the events that you've testified to here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: In my case, and in my capacity today in which I am testifying, Sredoje Lukic did not participate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we read very -- we read notification for this witness and there is no mention of the name of my client. 65 ter notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The witness has just in fact said Mr. Sredoje Lukic has nothing to do with the events he's testified about today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see no harm done. Now, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would just notified by my case manager as to page 56, lines 13, 14 and 15, we would like a read back of the translation. My case manager indicates some confusion over the words that were printed on the English translation compared to what the actual witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If it's more convenient I could ask the witness simply to answer the question again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You would like to have lines 13, 14 and 15 read back, you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You believe something was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Misinterpreted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Misinterpreted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, how is that to be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There is no B/C/S transcript so it's either to replay the tape and have it retranslated or I can ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm not sure how to do that, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think I'll have the question re-asked. Ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-014, there is some confusion about what your answer was to one of my questions so I'm just going to simply ask the question again. My question was: As you look at Milan Lukic today, is there anything that appears to you to be different from his appearance as you recall it on the 7th of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. I said -- I said there, when I was describing him, that he had brown hair, that he's tall, and then he was slimmer than he is now, but his features clearly show that that is him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you determine that he's slimmer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not now. He is heavier than he was then when he came to get me on the 7th of June. Now he is fatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you determine that he's fatter now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we can go back and forth like that, from today until tomorrow. I mean, I am saying that it is him. He's clearly recognizable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm quite entitled to ask the question. You say he's fatter now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's obvious to me that you're not seeing the entirety of his body. I'm asking you how are you able to determine that he's fatter now than at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, just by looking at his face. A man that is slim, his face is thin. When he gets fatter, the face gets fatter as well. He cannot just be a certain way in the bottom part of his body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That may be a plus for the Detention Unit. Now, I want to ask you another question. When was the last time that you saw Milan Lukic before today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he took me away on the 7th of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before the 7th of June 1992, when was the last time that you had seen Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a long time ago, during our school days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I'd like you to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time that he went to school with me together, until the second year more or less, when he left that school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, you told me that you were in school for two years together, 1984 and 1985. Counsel can correct me if that is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe it was '83 and '84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: '83 and '84. '83 and '84. So the last time that you saw Milan Lukic before the 7th of June 1992 was 1984?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: VG-014, you were born in 1967, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that would make you 41 years old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so how many years ago was 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: 16 years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was just wondering if he had a sense of time frame, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You hadn't had any opportunity between that time and this time to see photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I did have an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you have that opportunity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: The photographs from the wanted poster.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And where were those wanted posters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the posters or the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to know exactly all of the photographs you've ever seen of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you one thing. I would need to draw for you every building, any institution that was in charge of searching for those persons to indicate where the headquarters are, where the posters were pinned up in the corridor and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're saying that there were photographs all over the place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was all over the place, but I'm working at a place where they do have these photographs. I didn't say that this was in the place where I'm living.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Understood. So you would see these photos at work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: From time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't count how many times. Whenever I would pass a photo then I would see it. I can't tell you if I passed ten times or once or 15 times in the course of a week or a month. I didn't count that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long did you work at this place where you saw Milan's photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what other kinds of places were his photographs posted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Sir, I said clearly which places these were, the institutions that would be conducting investigations about war criminals, and I think it's very clear where these institutions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, they are not clear to me because I've never been there so I would ask that you make the Court clear as to where they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. But I cannot reveal my place of work, so I wouldn't want to do that. I still work there, so I wouldn't wish to disclose the place, the name of it or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We can go into private session for that and that's what I'd suggest. May we go into private session, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 14, now that we are in private session, tell me all the kinds of places that you would be able to see Mr. Lukic's photograph where you live?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in seeing these photographs, how old was Mr. Lukic in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't say. I don't know when they managed to take the photograph. There is no date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we can go back into public session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's fine, if that's what you would prefer, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you and he are the same age, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old were you in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: 23, I think, 23, 24, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So is the picture in the photograph a 23 year old Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it older?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you tell me approximately how much older?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Maybe five years or so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And but regardless you've had a lot of time to study the photograph of Milan Lukic over the years?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long had you worked there before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: A year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you've worked there approximately 11 years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, when we are calculating up to now, to 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, what have you reviewed -- well, you've had at least a meeting with Mr. Groome, correct, before today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Could you please clarify a little bit for me? I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the last meeting you've had with the Office of the Prosecutor before your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I think that it was the gentleman to my right, I don't know the name. He was the Prosecutor. I was with him a day or two ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I couldn't really say exactly. It was just getting to know one another, like an introduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that you'd met him before, during Mitar Vasiljevic's trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you didn't need to get to know him again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Does that have any -- that have anything to do with anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's a simple yes-or-no question, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I think that there was no need to get to know him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So did you review evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What did you review?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I just reminded myself about some details from my statement that I might have perhaps forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you given a copy of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have a copy of your statement before two days ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you retain a copy in your records since the Vasiljevic file?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No, I can't keep that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many times did you read your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Once was enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm assuming that you viewed the two photographs and the video that we saw in court today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you view any photographs of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you review any copies of your transcripts from earlier trials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before this meeting a couple days ago with the Prosecutor, when was the last time you met with other members of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you find out you were going to be coming to testify here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I got that from -- actually, I was informed about this from Sarajevo, which is the head of the UN office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you have a meeting for this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, from before the war, you indicated in your statement that you weren't political.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you did join the fight, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You joined the 11 of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you joined because you wanted to fight the Serbians, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. I didn't join because I wanted to fight the Serbians but for personal defence reasons, and for the purposes of defending my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And defending your countrymen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Defending your religion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before the war, you worked in a granite factory, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were a strong man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you worked for this granite firm after your compulsory training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And after high school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: After high school, I got a job at this construction company for the first time, and then there was a brief period when I went to serve my compulsory military term of duty, and then after I completed the military, I again got a job in the same company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the name of your high school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: You mean the name of the school, the building, or the name of my profession or my qualifications?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would prefer you answer both.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: That was the Hamid Besirevic High School centre which was in the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was asking whether we should have this in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I discussed the name with the witness before -- prior about the name of the company, he did not feel that jeopardized his security. There is only one school in Visegrad so I don't feel that that does, although I haven't specifically asked him that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the name of your profession that you studied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I was by profession or by trade a locksmith, and I had secondary school vocational qualifications for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, do you remember your teachers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: For example, now I know, because three or four years ago or two or three years ago I went to the high school centre because I needed to get my diploma; and I recognised a person by the name -- or nicknamed Koke, this was a Professor for physical education. I don't remember his first and last flame so when I say Koke those who knew the teachers would remember him. Now he's the director of the school. And well, who could remember these things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll just move on, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you say you knew Milan Lukic at school but you were never in class with him directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there were 300 to 400 students in each section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many sections were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I don't have that information. I wasn't interested in that. There were two shifts, the first and the second class shift. I don't know how many classes there were. We had locksmiths, electricians, plumbers. I don't need to name all of the vocations. It was something that I was never really interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is Lukic a common last name in the area where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is Milan a common last -- or a common first name in the area where you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, there are quite a few Milans also from where he hails, so there were quite a few. One couldn't call one's son Mustafa if he was stood up [as interpreted] Milan or Sredoje or Dragan what have you or what have you not; but I didn't count them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know many Milans around your age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I don't think that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So was Milan Lukic the only Milan you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you only knew of Milan Lukic, right? You didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: That is what you say. I have said that I knew him personally. I knew him from school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many times did you speak with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I cannot recall that now. There would be a day or two in succession that we would talk, and then we would not talk for a couple of days. There are some other colleagues with whom I socialised from Zupa, for instance, Boban Simsic was also a schoolmate of mine and there were others. I don't think I need list them all now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you said you -- you indicated on direct examination that he was -- you only knew of him but you didn't hang out with him or go places with him or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No, no. We didn't hang out. I did not keep company with him. I would never have kept company with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You never would have. Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I just would not. Seeing what he has done, every honour to him for that, but I cannot ever be his friend or comrade nor could I have been one then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I'd like to have this checked. Did I not ask the witness whether he had a speaking relationship with Milan Lukic? And I believe his answer was no. Do you remember my asking you that, Witness, whether you spoke with Milan Lukic? And your answer was no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, these talks that we had, those were not long talks of friends and comrades, perhaps we would pass by each other and say high or hello or goodbye. If that is considered a talk or a conversation, then let it be; but that's what it was about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Milan Lukic in school had Muslim friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, he probably had Muslim friends but he was no friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you see him hanging and keeping company with Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you said he was quiet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What do you mean by "quiet"? How would you describe a quiet person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, you see, these boys behaved in different ways. Some sought to provoke others and to -- were spoiling for a fight, and as far as I knew him, he was not like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that especially where religion and ethnicity came, there were tensions in high school amongst boys of different religions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. But it could not be observed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, were there ever fights at school between boys of different religions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, there were fights. You know, children will be children.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you never heard of Milan Lukic engaging in a fight of any kind, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you say that you know the village that Milan came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I know it slightly because for a certain period of time, while the long transmission line which passed through this village was being erected, I worked there for three or four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know Milan's family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know his father's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that it's customary that people in your country are known by their names and then who their father is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, yes, but at that time I was not interested in his father's name. I wasn't interested in him either. But ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, out of 300 to 400 students on your shift, he seemed to find the time to say hello to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: It wasn't only him. Boban Simsic and Suad Suceska and the Juso Puljo and the other school mates also would find the time to say hello to me, not only him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, not knowing him before that, wouldn't it seem like he might want to be your friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: It might have seemed that way at that time, but I just didn't manage to become friends with him, so it turned out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you had said a little earlier that you wouldn't become friends with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Let me tell you: Even today, as I speak, in 2008, I have very few friends. I'm not a person who is interested in having too many friends. I just have two to three genuine friends. I am not interested in other people in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the ethnic -- I'd like to go back to 1990. Where were you in 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: In 1990, I was in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the ethnic tensions, that's when you first noticed them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. When this multi-party system came into being, that is when they started.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why do you believe the multi-party system was the fault of the tensions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I will tell you why, because the parties that we had then were the SDA, the SDS, everyone wanted to be with his party and to head his party and then to do his own thing, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic left high school, and you're saying that he left early?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: At that time, there were these courses being organised for the police and that is probably when he left. I and a colleague of mine were teaching in Sarajevo, so he would probably not have gone to Sarajevo but elsewhere for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were teaching what in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: The -- I actually applied --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word is applied, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- applied for the police academy that was at the end of the second year of secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you assumed that Milan Lukic also applied at the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: It was not that you applied every secondary school, you applied at the police academy, whoever wished to attend it, like myself, I wanted to attend it in Sarajevo, but then I did so in Obrenovac and that's the way it worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we have to take a break now. Before we take the break, however, Mr. Groome, there is a matter relating to the next witness you wanted some guidance as to what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the witness flew in and it's here, if it seems unlikely the witness will be called today, we would like him to be sent to the hotel and have him here this of tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer will you be in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm not real sure, but I think it's probably most prudent to send the witness to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. You may do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We break now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise, could I please make correction for the transcript, last admitted the video, was Exhibit P4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to bring the Court's attention to another exception to the transcript, namely page 58, line 23, when we did re-issue the question to the witness or Mr. Groome reissued the question as to the identification, and what was on the translation was, "I am saying that it is him" and it is our position that a phrase was left off the end of that that said, "Let it be him." And we would like to check the tape of the transcript to verify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're saying that left off the transcript was a phrase coming at the end of that sentence as follows: "Let it be him"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, maybe it was left off as a repeated word but we believe it is a phrase that carries a bit more significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll have that checked but not now. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, back to 1990, when the two party system began, did you -- you still of course were -- had your allegiance to your own ethnicity and your own religion, would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you did foresee a war occurring, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You thought it would be only 15 to 20 days, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Arms were being distributed to the Serbians, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You stated in your statement that you could hear training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How do you know it was training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I shall clarify it for you. I lived in a section of Bikavac by the road. My house was by the road. And the training ground for shooting ground was at Ban Polje, which is a place some -- about one kilometre away from Bikavac. So you know yourself when there are exercises of the reserve force of the Yugoslav army, they would mobilize both Serbs and Muslims, all those who formed part of the reserve force of the then-JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, but at that time, we were not called up but the Serbs were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But with regard to the distribution of arms, you didn't see this distribution, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You only heard about it from colleagues, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And these colleagues were political, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did they join the army or the resistance with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Probably, they probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you stated in your original statement that you believed the Serbs wanted war, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But wouldn't that be an unfair generality of Serbians to say they wanted war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, you see, that is my opinion, that I conveyed to you what was my perception. Now, whether it was fair or not, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to stay around this time, as we went on the break, you stated that you went to the police academy in Sarajevo first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. That is not what I said. I didn't say that I went there. What I said was that I was submitting my application for the police academy in Sarajevo, but I didn't go there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then you went to Obrenovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that I went to Obrenovac. What I said was that Lukic was in Obrenovac. Not me. I would never go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it your opinion that Lukic was in Obrenovac, or is it a fact that you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. It is an assumption on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how would you make this assumption? What information came to you that would give you this assumption?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I cannot remember on what I based it. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A long time ago, as in when you were 17 years old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I expect so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that a 17 year old is too young to become a policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, sir, can I ask a question? Are you interested in my past or in something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm interested in what you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether I was too young, but in the note of refusal that I received from the police academy, they stated that I was two months too old; so you can now interpret it as you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that there is only -- you're only one date that you can become a police officer and you're too young or too old other than that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I did not quite get your question but let me try to answer you. When I was applying for the police academy, at that time, I was two months older than the required age. My colleague, who applied with me, he was admitted. Now, whether they had some date standards, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, going back to 1990 to 1992, after the elections and the tensions, you were hearing stories about the Green Berets, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. These stories actually were being told by the Serbs, that there were Green Berets perpetrating genocide around Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the Green Berets were a Muslim force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. That's what they called them, the Serbs, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but you -- what are the Green Berets to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: For me, the Green Berets did not exist at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They didn't exist at all, you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when the Uzice Corps entered, you stated in your statement that they found no evidence of the Green Berets committing genocide?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How do you know what evidence they had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, if there are no victims, if there were no casualties, if there were no people taken away, if there were no people executed, what proof what evidence should there exist for one to establish that a genocide had been committed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How do you know there was no people taken away or genocide or executions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I just do know, because we did not have that kind of weaponry in order to be able to commit anything of the kind, and you know that we are not a people who seek revenge or want to exterminate others or anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you say "we" are not a people, who are you describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't say "we are not a people." I said "we are a people." I mean, us, the Muslim people, is a people that does not want revenge or extermination or anything similar, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you aware of what's going on in Baghdad today between the Shia and the Sunni?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I don't follow that, and I'm not really that interested either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You don't watch the news?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours as to relevance of what's going on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, where are you taking this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He answered no that he didn't watch the news, judge. I think from a credibility perspective I have to let the answer stand. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now in your statement you described that the conflict was like two goats fighting, one with horns and one without horns.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's because you stated the Muslims did not have weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that your opinion, or is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, at this time, you were not part of the war, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have anything to fight with at that time. We could have been a part of the war if somebody made some kind of device or an explosive device or something similar. Had we had weapons that the Serbs had, it would have been different, but we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in fact, you stated there was a Muslim resistance that made their own bombs and weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you part of this resistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how would you know if they had bombs or weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, somebody who had money bought a rifle. I didn't have a rifle so I couldn't be a part of the resistance. How could I be a part of it? I wasn't going to strangle people with my bare hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I didn't ask you if you had a rifle. I asked you how you knew if they had bombs and weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: If something happened at your neighbour's you would know that it happened. If he had planted a field of potatoes, you would know that. Anything like that. If somebody made a bomb, it was known that they did that and they would say, "Well, I also have it if I need it." It's like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A bomb is not something that you use when you need it. A bomb is something that's planted to blow up people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, again, how would you know that your neighbour has a bomb unless you're part of the resistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Maybe I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because the resistance is a secret society, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Perhaps it wasn't secret, as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And to certain governments, resistance that uses bombs are considered terrorists.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, let me say this: The destruction of civilians by long-range weapons, taking them away, executing them, is also a part of that so you cannot tell me something -- about something that I did and that I was a part of in order to defend myself, without talking about the other side that was trying to destroy the Muslim people, so we have to have some kind of balance or look at both sides in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you felt justified using bombs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, and any weapon that anyone had, it was justified for them to use it then at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Even against Serbian civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: The Muslims are not a people that were destroying civilians. We went to the lines and we were fighting soldier-to-soldier. We did not destroy civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How can you use a bomb fighting soldier-to-soldier?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I'm not sure that I understand where you are going with this line of questioning. What are you trying to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm trying to establish that the witness was, in fact, part of the militia, part of the violence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- questions that relate more directly to that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I said put questions that relate more directly to that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the use of shelling enraged you as a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: It enraged us -- or everything enraged us, the shelling, the burnings, the taking away of civilians, of women, children. It all enraged us. And you should see if something like that would enrage you as well. So can you please take that into consideration and not try to twist things around so that instead of Milan Lukic being guilty, you're trying to make me guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that as the last time you saw Milan Lukic in high school, as far as you knew, he was guilty of nothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: How do you mean he was guilty of nothing? Then, at school, or now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: At school, well, what was he supposed to have been guilty of?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Violence against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Who, when they were at -- as a child then, would even think of any kind of persecution or racism? All we thought of was to finish our school. We didn't think about anything like if a person liked or disliked Muslims or Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But a 16 year old can raise his hand against a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. A 16 year old Muslim could raise his hand against a Serb, but things like that didn't happen then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You indicated there were fights in school between ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, was I supposed to be a referee or something?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You indicated that Milan Lukic had never been part of those ethnic fights.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't see anything like that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you did see him with Muslim friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he said hi to you, regularly, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you had to leave your home in the spring of 1992, how did that make you feel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to put the same question to you. How would you feel if you had to leave your own home?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, in the Court, you're not allowed to put questions. Your role is to answer questions. If the questions are improper, then I will stop counsel. Now, proceed, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You must have felt helpless.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't get the question. I didn't hear it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You must have been angry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. Angry and dejected. I don't know how I can explain to you how a person feels when they have to leave their home; I can explain how they feel and how that whole thing looks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Probably made you want to fight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Had there been an opportunity, perhaps I would have fought.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you left right before the Uzice forces returned or came into Visegrad, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, that evening I left Visegrad and the Uzice Corps entered Visegrad the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This was March, April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, up to that point, would it be fair to say that the Muslim community was a close community there, even under the sense of persecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this is how stories and -- would come through the community was through word of mouth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And between the last time you saw Milan Lukic and leaving the first time from Visegrad, you had not heard Milan Lukic's name in any bad light, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: That period, and when the JNA was still there, I didn't hear him mentioned anywhere except for the case that I mentioned before. I don't need to repeat it, the case of Behija Zukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long had you known Ms. Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Ms. Zukic had her shop, and the shop was very close to the cultural hall, and when I went to elementary school, the Vuk Karadzic elementary school in Pionirska Street, I would pass by that shop twice a day and I would go in there and buy cookies or whatever I needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you had known this woman since you were a young boy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And she had been nice to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I don't have the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: She had always treated you -- you felt special when you were in her shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. It was a very -- she was a very nice woman, very pleasant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And again, it enraged you when she was found to have been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Of course. Anybody would be enraged when somebody killed such a pleasant, such a dear, nice woman; that person would have to be a monster to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you didn't see the circumstances of this killing, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You only heard about it through colleagues, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in your mind, after hearing the stories, Milan Lukic was guilty of that death, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were certain of this in your heart, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if you could get revenge for that, you would, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, when you join an army, you join an army to defend your countrymen, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, the 11th of June 1992 was when I joined the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if a soldier on the other side in a battle kills your friend, that soldier may not die until another day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Nor do I. Please move on. Unless you can clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you fight in war, people die every day, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And one day, your own friend, your comrade in arms, might die at your side, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you may not be able to kill the person that killed your friend that day, but you'll go to war the next day and maybe you'll be able to, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And even though it's done under the colour of war, isn't that in a sense revenge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: When you are attacked by someone, you are forced to defend yourself. Who is going to kill who first is something that depends on skill.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, with Ms. Zukic, I'd like to go back a little bit before she died. Isn't it true that the Uzice forces were committing atrocities, in your eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you left right as those forces entered Visegrad, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes, but for safety reasons, not knowing what would happen once the Uzice Corps came in. I didn't know in I would be taken away, killed, if I would be detained, questioned. I left my house for safety reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you left, your house was unmolested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: When I left, I left the house the way it was but when I returned, I didn't find the house in the same state that I left it in. It had been broken into and ransacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in fact most of the Muslim homes had been ransacked, burned or violated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And one common thing was that the army was in the town during that time of vandalism?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true, in times of war, that police generally come under the jurisdiction of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that as you went through check-points, you saw members of both the army and local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that the army appeared to control the local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: I didn't have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the army appeared to control the local Serbs that were at the check-points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No. They didn't control Serbs but Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood my question. So I'll go back through it. Isn't it true that at the check-points, the check-points were manned by both army and local Serbians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes. They were manned by the soldiers and the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the local Serbs were also wearing army uniforms, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And some of them were in police uniforms, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you knew they were locals simply because you recognised them, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because Visegrad is still a relatively small community, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during the time before you decided to flee, check-points had been around for a long while, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: When I left, if you're thinking of when I left my house, there were no check-points then, but when I returned to the house, that's when the check-points had been set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This has to be your last question for the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you went through several check-points just to get home, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you never saw, amongst the local Serbians, Milan Lukic, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will break here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of July, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
